title: Who's Who: Rafael Soria
summary: Missing persons investigator whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Rafael Soria (born 1844) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a missing persons investigator whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Soria investigates disappearances near unstable apertures and insists on ordinary evidence before attributing a case to the Stratum. He introduced paired departure registers to catch discrepancies between what travelers intended and what the instruments recorded.
His unresolved files have made him a familiar and uneasy figure in Alderwick’s want-ad pages.

For Alderwick readers, Rafael Soria stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
